title: Valid Parentheses
statement: Given a string `s` containing only the characters `()[]{}`, determine whether the input string is valid. A string is valid when every open bracket is closed by the same type of bracket, and brackets are closed in the correct order.

examples.explanation: Every bracket is matched in order.
The closing bracket does not match the open one.
Correctly matched types, but interleaved rather than nested.

optimalComplexity: O(n) time, O(n) space — a single stack pass.
rubric: Uses a stack. A counter alone cannot handle mixed bracket types.
Returns false on a closing bracket when the stack is empty.
Returns false at the end if the stack is not empty — this is the most commonly missed case.
Handles the empty string as valid.
followUps: What if the string could also contain other characters that should be ignored?
What is the minimum number of insertions needed to make the string valid?
Can you do it without a stack if there is only one bracket type?
similarProblems: Minimum Remove to Make Valid Parentheses
